entries.justification: Registered product and company names are intentionally not translated.
Standalone industry terms approved by the French glossary remain unchanged.
Parser names, file extensions and executable shell identifiers are code tokens and must not be translated.
Provider model display names are registered product/SKU identifiers; translating them would make model selection ambiguous.
This coordinated legacy component is absent from the active route graph; /pricing renders the fully localized EcodeProductMarketingPages implementation and a regression test enforces that boundary.
These are canonical server-to-agent role identifiers used in English prompts; api.chat maps every role title to localized UI copy before emitting annotations.
This dependency-free state model only returns invariant diagnostics to assertions/tests; no raw message is rendered in the IDE.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Workflow is disabled\.|Nested workflow depth limit reached|Workflow task has no command|Target workflow \{…\} was not found|Nested workflow "\{…\}" failed|Command exited with \{…\}|Schedule is empty\.|Cron must have 5 fields: minute hour day month weekday\.|Invalid value in cron field \{…\}: "\{…\}"\.)$
entries.justification: The orchestration messages are matched and replaced with apiRuntimeRoutes locale copy before IDE-panel serialization. Cron parser diagnostics are consumed only as validity signals; the route emits its localized EMPTY_CRON_SCHEDULE/INVALID_CRON_SCHEDULE contract instead.
The IDE-panel route always replaces this structural default with localized security finding copy before persisting or returning it.
Preview catches every capture failure and emits the localized thumbnailFailed message; cancellation remains silent and raw capture diagnostics are never rendered.
This Error is an internal stream-cancellation sentinel. The gateway catches it and emits localized provider stream copy; the sentinel text is never serialized.

entries.textPattern: ^Pod spec changed in an immutable field.*recreating the pod\.$
entries.justification: This structured operator warning is written only to service logs. Workspace start failures cross the HTTP boundary through the localized public error catalogue.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:workspace registry at .* is corrupted \(invalid JSON\): .*|workspace registry at .* is corrupted \(expected a JSON array, got .*\)|server deployment not found: .*|Timed out waiting for pod .* to terminate before recreation|Pod .* was not ready before timeout|agent health responded .*)$
entries.justification: These messages carry file paths, pod names, deployment ids or upstream status solely for manager control flow and operator logs. The activate route maps its coded 404 to catalogued copy, while the global handler masks every uncaught 5xx with localized public copy.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Workspace not found|WORKSPACE_AGENT_TOKEN_SECRET is required|DATABASE_URL is required to start workspace-manager in production.*)$
entries.justification: The environment failures abort service startup before an HTTP server exists. The Prisma P2025 diagnostic is intercepted by the workspace-manager error handler and masked with localized public copy.
These legacy URL-embedded payload helpers have no production callers; the active share flow uses a server-minted token and maps every failure to clientRuntime.share locale copy.
This legacy update helper has no production imports; the active Update tab uses /api/update and localized updateTab copy.
The retired SwitchableStream implementation has no imports; api.chat now streams through mergeIntoDataStream and serializes localized stable error codes.
This is a developer-only React composition invariant caught by panel error recovery; it is never used as rendered copy.
This is a developer-only missing-provider invariant handled by the localized route or panel boundary and never rendered verbatim.
This helper marks impossible TypeScript control-flow states; panel error boundaries render localized recovery copy instead of the diagnostic.
No production route imports this retired copied-shell loader; marketing.$slug now re-exports the localized HTTP 404 and a regression test enforces the boundary.
Reserved example.test host suffix is a code or domain token and must remain unchanged.
This scanner match is the generated DOM id for the message field, not rendered copy; translating it would break label and input wiring.
The interpolated title comes from the active locale catalogue; only the non-translatable E-Code brand suffix is static.
These values are internal route ids used only to index localized admin section titles; they are never rendered as labels.
ms and HTTP are invariant technical units/protocol identifiers; the numeric value is locale-formatted before interpolation.
The section title and fallback are resolved from the request locale; only the non-translatable E-Code brand suffix is static.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:PREVIEW_TENANT_SECRET is required when PREVIEW_PROXY_ENFORCE_TENANT is enabled\.|PREVIEW_ENFORCE_PRIVATE_PORTS requires API_BASE_URL, PREVIEW_PROXY_SHARED_SECRET and PREVIEW_TENANT_SECRET\.|WORKSPACE_MANAGER_URL is required in production for preview-proxy\.|PREVIEW_PROXY_SHARED_SECRET is required in production for preview-proxy\.|WORKSPACE_MANAGER_URL must be an absolute URL in production for preview-proxy\.|WORKSPACE_MANAGER_URL must use HTTPS or an internal Kubernetes service DNS URL in production\.|WORKSPACE_MANAGER_URL must not point to localhost in production\.)$
entries.justification: These configuration invariants abort preview-proxy construction before the public Fastify server is available. Runtime HTTP/HTML failures use the locale-aware public catalogue and never serialize these operator diagnostics.
This module is imported only by readme-accuracy.spec.ts and returns CI assertion diagnostics about stale documentation. It has no production import and cannot be rendered by the preview proxy.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:SIEM webhook \{…\} is missing an encrypted signing secret|SIEM webhook delivery failed: \{…\}|WORKSPACE_MANAGER_URL is required to trigger workspace\.gc|workspace\.gc upstream failed: \{…\}|API_INTERNAL_URL \(or API_URL\) is required to trigger (?:inactivity\.gc|metering\.objectStorage|metering\.databaseStorage|database\.maintenance)|(?:inactivity\.gc|metering\.objectStorage|metering\.databaseStorage|database\.maintenance) upstream failed: \{…\}|Unsupported (?:workspace|enterprise|deploy) job: \{…\})$
entries.justification: These errors are BullMQ control-plane failure reasons and operator diagnostics. No application route reads worker queues or failedReason; user-facing scheduled-task and deployment state is persisted and localized by the API catalogue.
These values are emitted only as structured process lifecycle logs to stdout and have no UI consumer or HTTP response path.
These uppercase values are stable deployment state-machine codes, not rendered prose. The API keeps the code invariant and localizes the accompanying deployment logs/message at response time.
These uppercase values are stable server-deployment transfer codes and must remain language-independent. Public deployment records localize the accompanying text separately.
These uppercase values are stable deployment error codes consumed by clients and automation. They are intentionally not translated; user-facing messages and logs are localized independently.
This secret-strength invariant aborts service construction before Fastify accepts traffic. Locale-aware proxy errors use stable codes and the public catalogue.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:No connection found for the supplied userConnectionId\.|The connection does not belong to the workspace user\.|Connection status is \{…\}; reconnection required\.|This connection is reserved for direct user operations and is not exposed to the agent\.|This project is not linked to the supplied connection\.|The connection owner is no longer a member of the organization\.|\{…\} is disabled by an administrator for this organization\.|Your organization role is not permitted to use \{…\}\.|No access token is stored for this connection\.|Stored access token could not be decrypted with the current ENCRYPTION_SECRET\.)$
entries.justification: These resolver diagnostics stay inside the connector-proxy trust boundary. The proxy deliberately ignores `resolution.error`/`detail` and maps only the stable code through public-i18n; integration tests prove resolver secrets are not serialized.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Reconnect \{…\}|Your \{…\} connection\{…\} needs to be reconnected — its access was revoked or expired\.)$
entries.justification: These English values are backward-compatible database fallbacks stored with `notifications.connectionReconnectRequired` plus provider/account parameters. The API's publicNotification serializer always resolves that descriptor in the request locale before returning the feed.

These values are TypeScript media-error discriminants passed to setMediaError. The component renders only the localized catalogue entry selected by that code; the codes themselves never appear in the DOM.
This value is a CSS custom-property reference used for the incident severity color, not rendered language copy.

The capture endpoint is a private in-cluster service contract. ThumbnailCapture consumes only PNG bytes, swallows every non-2xx response and logs the status; public thumbnail refresh routes return their own locale-aware stable contract, so these internal diagnostics cannot reach the UI.

entries.textPattern: ^Unknown provider '\{…\}' — add it to the keyword catalog or provide a custom one\.$
entries.justification: createConnectionRequestDataPart is called only by api.chat's connector annotation loop, which catches this catalog-drift invariant and skips the annotation without serializing the diagnostic. Provider names and connector cards use the locale catalog.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:No models found for provider \{…\}|No user message found)$
entries.justification: createSummary and selectContext run inside api.chat's context-optimization recovery block, which emits localized contextOptimizationSkipped copy. streamText failures are classified and localized by api.chat/api.llmcall/api.enhancer, while api.agent.self-repair returns its localized SELF_REPAIR_FAILED code; no raw diagnostic is serialized.

getManagedCredentials catches this private control-plane status before it leaves the module, logs an operator warning and returns the last cache or environment fallback. It is never attached to an HTTP or stream payload.

The production disclosure builder opens only keys derived from its own byName map, and openResource has no production caller. These exceptions protect programmer invariants; the values cannot reach a rendered response.

Provider-list methods receive provider instances from this manager's registry; api.models also validates a requested provider before calling them and masks its outer failure with MODEL_CATALOG_UNAVAILABLE. The empty-registry error is a startup/programming invariant handled by localized route and panel boundaries.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Failed to fetch \{…\} models: \{…\} \{…\}|Failed to fetch models from Google API: \{…\} \{…\}|Invalid response format from Google API|No baseUrl found for (?:LMStudio|Ollama) provider|HTTP \{…\}: \{…\}|Failed to fetch models: \{…\} \{…\})$
entries.justification: Every dynamic provider discovery call is invoked through LLMManager.updateModelList/getModelListFromProvider, whose per-provider catch logs the failure and returns an empty dynamic list; providers that catch internally do the same. api.models returns localized static fallbacks and never serializes these diagnostics.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Missing API key for \{…\} provider|Missing configuration for \{…\} provider|Missing Api Key configuration for \{…\} provider|Invalid API key format for \{…\} provider|Invalid API key format for \{…\}\. Expected: id\.secret|Failed to generate JWT token: \{…\})$
entries.justification: Provider-instance failures are private diagnostics used for status classification. api.chat, api.llmcall and api.enhancer map them to locale catalog copy; agent mode/planning catches and falls back; api.agent.self-repair returns localized SELF_REPAIR_FAILED. No route serializes the raw provider message.

These are internal dynamic-model label frames, not product names. api.models runs every returned model through localizeModelInfo before serializing it, translating Dynamic/context/by and input/output prices with French number spacing; targeted route tests cover each frame. Other LLM consumers use the labels only for internal model selection.
These values are TypeScript render-state discriminants passed to setStatus. The component selects localized loading/error copy from chat-renderers and never renders the discriminant itself.
These are exact GitHub OAuth scope identifiers. They are code-like permission names and must remain unchanged so administrators can compare them with GitHub configuration.
The placeholder contains conventional directory and file identifiers for .gitignore input; translating them would produce invalid ignore patterns.
This scanner match is a Tailwind CSS class token used to color the status indicator, not rendered prose.
This is an i18next lookup key used to retrieve localized error-level copy; the key itself is never rendered.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:ENOENT: no such file or directory, stat '\{…\}'|EINVAL: invalid argument, readlink '\{…\}'|EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink '\{…\}' -> '\{…\}')$
entries.justification: These are Node-compatible filesystem protocol diagnostics required by isomorphic-git. Callers use errno/code for control flow and all user feedback is mapped through localized Git panel copy; file paths and protocol identifiers must not be translated.
These are merge-content state discriminants. GitTab checks only whether the code exists and renders idePanels.git.conflictLoadFailed plus localized retry copy; the codes never enter the DOM.

These values are stable server-only telemetry codes. projects.new reads only allowed/checked/reason and renders localized moderation-category copy; provider diagnostics and response bodies are never returned to the browser.
These typed values are i18n catalogue keys stored in component state. The route renders only copy[status], so the key string never reaches the DOM.
These values are LoadErrorKind discriminants. ConnectedResourceBoundary maps them to accountSettingsConnected localized descriptions and never renders the codes.
These placeholders are exact OAuth scope identifiers administrators must copy unchanged into provider configuration; translating them would create invalid scopes.
vck_ is the immutable technical prefix of E-Code API keys. The ellipsis masks secret material and the prefix must remain byte-identical.
This is an internal fallback code passed into classifyDatabaseRestoreError. The classifier discards its message field and always returns apiRuntime.snapshot localized copy.
These are the two explicitly locale-selected SEO title frames in the route meta function; each request receives only its active locale and the E-Code brand remains unchanged.
These are typed draft-error discriminants. The form maps each code to organizationSecurity.ipAllowlist localized validation copy before rendering.
These are exact DNS record names and verification-token formats. They are displayed in monospace for copying and must not be translated or altered.
The interpolated post title is already selected from the locale-specific blog data. E-Code Blog is the unchanged branded suffix, not untranslated prose.
WAL LSN is the canonical PostgreSQL write-ahead-log sequence-number identifier followed by its technical value; translating it would make diagnostics ambiguous.
This is a Tailwind/CSS custom-property class used to color error log rows, not text rendered to the user.

decodeBase32 receives only platform-generated/decrypted TOTP secrets. A corrupt stored secret is a server invariant; API auth routes return their localized stable MFA contract and the global 5xx handler never serializes this diagnostic.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Concurrent published-app limit reached \(\{…\}\)\.|Quota exceeded for \{…\}|Missing Stripe signature|Invalid Stripe signature header|Expired Stripe signature|Invalid Stripe signature|Stripe request failed: \{…\})$
entries.justification: Every coded billing exception crosses services/api through its locale-aware error handler. app-public-copy has anchored EN/FR templates for APP_LIMIT, QUOTA and every Stripe signature/request variant; tests prove interpolation and French output.
StripeClient.ping returns this only as an internal diagnostic. /admin/stripe-health logs a redacted detail and always emits STRIPE_HEALTH_REQUEST_FAILED from the locale catalogue, never result.error.
vCPU and GiB are invariant compute-unit identifiers. Numbers are formatted at the presentation boundary; translating the units would make machine SKUs ambiguous.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Missing connector catalog copy: \{…\}|Missing connector API key field copy: \{…\}\.\{…\})$
entries.justification: These fail the operator-only Prisma seed when its bilingual source catalogue is incomplete. The script has no HTTP/runtime import, so the diagnostics cannot render in the platform.

entries.textPattern: ^DATABASE_URL is required for the persistent Prisma/PostgreSQL store\.$
entries.justification: This configuration invariant aborts database-client construction during service startup. No public server exists on that path; runtime API failures are masked by locale-aware service boundaries.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Node pool "\{…\}" is at \{…\}/\{…\} nodes|\(\{…\}% of the autoscaling max\)\.|The pool cannot scale further — raise the max node count\.|Approaching the ceiling — consider raising the max node count\.|Reserved CPU on "\{…\}" is \{…\}% of allocatable —|new workspaces may fail to schedule\. Free idle workspaces or raise the autoscaling max\.)$
entries.justification: /admin/capacity discards every raw CapacityAlert.message and rebuilds it from kind, level and numeric capacity through CAPACITY_* EN/FR catalogue entries. Targeted tests prove both alert variants.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:nixStoreGenerationHash must be sha256:<64 hex>, got "\{…\}"|Workspace images must be pinned in production|kubectl get \{…\}/\{…\} returned unparseable JSON|kubectl get \{…\} -l \{…\} returned unparseable JSON)$
entries.justification: These are control-plane manifest/configuration diagnostics carrying hashes, image policy or kubectl selectors. Workspace-manager catches them behind stable localized public errors; services/api also masks every uncaught 5xx.
Only source-defined metric names/types reach this registry assertion. Violations are programmer/operator diagnostics written to service logs; no metrics endpoint serializes Error.message.
assertWithinQuota attaches QUOTA_EXCEEDED; the API error boundary maps the anchored template through app-public-copy for French and never displays a raw key.
requirePermission attaches RBAC_FORBIDDEN. API routes localize the stable code and the global French fallback masks any unmatched permission diagnostic.
The runtime id is platform configuration, not user copy. Callers keep SANDBOX_RUNTIME_UNKNOWN as a machine code and locale-aware HTTP boundaries mask the operator diagnostic.

entries.textPattern: ^ObjectStorageClient: (?:apiUrl is required \(set OBJECT_STORAGE_API_URL or pass apiUrl\)\.|accessToken is required \(set OBJECT_STORAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN or pass accessToken\)\.|projectId is required \(set PROJECT_ID or pass projectId\)\.|no fetch implementation available; pass options\.fetch\.)$
entries.justification: These are developer exceptions from the private generated-app SDK, containing exact constructor/environment identifiers. They are not an E-Code HTTP/DOM surface and translating the code identifiers would make remediation unsafe.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:\{…\} must be set when NODE_ENV=production|CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY is required in production|Invalid encrypted payload)$
entries.justification: Production-secret checks abort startup; invalid ciphertext is caught inside connector/config trust boundaries and mapped to stable localized public errors. Raw secret/config diagnostics are never serialized.
assertCsrf attaches CSRF_REQUIRED; services/api's locale-aware error handler returns localized public copy/generic fallback, not this internal diagnostic.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Missing gallery metadata copy: \{…\}|Gallery demo application has no snapshot: \{…\}|Gallery metadata has no definition: \{…\})$
entries.justification: The immutable gallery catalogue is assembled at module startup from source-owned ids. Missing copy/snapshot definitions abort startup and cannot become an HTTP payload.

WorkspaceAgentClient has no production instantiation; workspace-manager/agent import only token/event helpers. Active agent calls use localized service contracts, so this private SDK exception cannot render.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:real skill failed to parse: \{…\}|fixture failed to parse: \{…\})$
entries.justification: This executable is an operator/CI proof script, not imported by the API. Its parse assertions print only to the invoking terminal.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:metadata token request failed \(\{…\}\)|metadata token response had no access_token)$
entries.justification: Metadata token errors are caught inside runAppImageBuild and reduced to an internal failed result. The deploy route persists only catalogued image progress and a generic localized DEPLOY_SERVER_FAILED log.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Cloud Build auth unavailable \(\{…\}\)|Cloud Build create failed \(\{…\}\): \{…\}|Cloud Build create failed \(\{…\}\)|Cloud Build create returned no build id|Image build \{…\}\{…\})$
entries.justification: These details only control the serverError failure branch; they are never appended to deployment logs or responses. User-visible [image] progress now uses APP_IMAGE_BUILD_* EN/FR catalogue templates and terminal failure uses DEPLOY_SERVER_FAILED.
shardForTenant is called with source/config-derived positive shard counts. This assertion protects deterministic internal placement and is never serialized by a route.
ManagerK8sPort statuses remain within the database control plane. API 5xx handling logs them and emits localized generic/database contracts; no response returns Error.message directly.

entries.textPattern: ^REDIS_URL is required to enqueue a deploy build$
entries.justification: The queue factory attaches DEPLOY_QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE. API failures cross the localized global handler; the environment diagnostic is retained only in operator logs.

These uppercase values are stable stream state-machine codes, introduced to prevent upstream/English exception text from entering localized deployment logs. The surrounding deployment log frame is localized at response time.

entries.textPattern: ^Deployment provider "\{…\}" is not configured for production use$
entries.justification: assertDeploymentProviderConfigured has no production caller; active deployment creation uses deployProviderConfigError(locale) and returns catalogued provider-specific copy.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:EMAIL_FROM is required in production when EMAIL_HTTP_ENDPOINT is configured\.|EMAIL_HTTP_ENDPOINT is required for HttpEmailProvider\.|EMAIL_HTTP_TOKEN is required in production when EMAIL_HTTP_ENDPOINT is configured\.|Email provider failed: \{…\}|EMAIL_HTTP_ENDPOINT \(Resend\) is required in production for transactional email\.)$
entries.justification: Configuration failures abort provider creation/startup; delivery failures are 5xx internal diagnostics. Transactional routes use the locale-aware error handler and never serialize the provider status text.

entries.textPattern: ^OAUTH_STATE_SECRET or JWT_SECRET must be set in production$
entries.justification: The missing signing secret aborts OAuth-state construction in production; callbacks otherwise return localized OAUTH_STATE_INVALID and never expose this configuration diagnostic.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:committed \{…\} must be within \[0, max \{…\}\]|tax \{…\} must be within \[0, committed \{…\}\]|taxPayableAccountId is required when taxMinor > 0|compensation requires a positive committed amount)$
entries.justification: These protect internal double-entry construction after validated billing calculations. Violations are programmer/accounting invariants handled as masked 5xx responses; values are never rendered as UI copy.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Invalid \{…\} field: empty list entry\.|Invalid \{…\} field: "\{…\}"\.|Invalid step in \{…\} field: "\{…\}"\.|Invalid range in \{…\} field: "\{…\}"\.|Invalid \{…\} value: "\{…\}"\.|\{…\} out of range \(\{…\}-\{…\}\): "\{…\}"\.|Inverted range in \{…\} field: "\{…\}"\.|Schedule is empty\.|A cron schedule needs exactly 5 fields \(minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week\); got \{…\}\.|This schedule never fires \(no matching date\)\.)$
entries.justification: parseCron diagnostics are consumed only as validity/control signals. validateSchedule and /scheduled-tasks/preview now emit SCHEDULE_INVALID_CRON or SCHEDULE_NEVER_FIRES through app-public-copy; raw parser text never crosses HTTP.
These are stable revision state-machine codes. Accompanying messages come from app-public-copy and deployment records localize them at response time.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:No package\.json found — cannot determine how to start this app\.|package\.json is not a JSON object\.|package\.json is not valid JSON\.|This looks like a static single-page app \(Vite/CRA with no server\)\. Deploy it as a Static site —|a server deploy needs a process that listens on a port\.|Detected \{…\} but couldn't find an entry point\. Add a "start" script \(e\.g\. "node server\.js"\)|or a "main" field to package\.json\.|Could not determine how to start this app: no "start" script, no "main" entry, and no recognized framework\.|Add a "start" script to package\.json \(e\.g\. "node server\.js"\)\.)$
entries.justification: detectServerRuntime now exposes stable codes only to the public deploy-target mapper. /deployments/detect and creation rebuild localized reason/error text through deploy-target-public/app-public-copy and mask raw diagnostics; targeted API tests cover FR.
Audit codes are source-defined alongside complete EN/FR JSON copy and validated by tests. A missing entry is a programmer invariant before any audit record/response is built.
This proof-oriented disclosure session has no production import; only its spec and operator proof script instantiate it. The exceptions cannot enter an API response.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Reconnect \{…\}|Your \{…\} connection\{…\} needs to be reconnected — its access was revoked or expired\.)$
entries.justification: These are backward-compatible database fallbacks stored with notifications.connectionReconnectRequired plus provider/account params. services/api publicNotification always resolves that messageKey in the active request locale.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:API_INTERNAL_URL, API_URL, SAAS_API_URL or API_BASE_URL is required to trigger deploy jobs|deploy\.(?:build|reap) upstream failed: \{…\})$
entries.justification: These become BullMQ failedReason/operator logs only. No application route reads failedReason; deployment state/logs are persisted by the API and localized through the deployment catalogue.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:--data must be valid JSON: \{…\}|--queue is required|--job is required|Unknown queue '\{…\}'\. Known queues: \{…\}|REDIS_URL is required to enqueue)$
entries.justification: enqueue-cli is invoked only by Kubernetes CronJobs/operators and exits to stderr; it has no HTTP/UI import. Flags, queue ids and environment-variable names are operational identifiers.
These discriminants are consumed only by attachment control flow and tests. The same result carries a separately catalogued EN/FR message, which is the only value passed to the composer toast.
These values are parser discriminants, not labels. The Secrets panel resolves them through localized copy before presenting a skipped-line explanation; the pasted line itself remains user content.
This is a structured server-log dimension emitted when usage recording has no auth context. It never crosses the route response or rendered chat stream.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Complex build request detected; split the work into specialist lanes and integrate the result before responding\.|Single-lane response is sufficient for this request\.)$
entries.justification: These are stable planner outcomes. api.chat passes the value through localizeApiChatOrchestrationReason before writing the orchestration annotation, so the English protocol source is never rendered verbatim in French.
These stable reason identifiers are emitted only as opt.routing telemetry and asserted in routing tests. They are not UI labels or response copy.
These discriminants select operator logging branches. api.bug-report returns the same localized BUG_REPORT_NOT_CONFIGURED contract for either case and never serializes the discriminant.
N/A is the approved language-neutral unavailable token for provider-owned model metadata; the same invariant token is defined in the model API locale catalogue.

This fallback is nested inside a private JWT-generation exception. Provider errors are caught by the chat route and replaced with localized stable error copy; the diagnostic is retained only for operator logs.
plan is a stable agent-mode gate discriminant; the other values are structured cache/summary telemetry reasons. None is rendered as user copy.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Auto-accept is disabled\.|\{…\} diagnostic error\(s\) must be fixed first\.|Run a real test command before auto-accept can apply all proposals\.|Run tests again after the latest AI proposal before auto-accept can continue\.|Latest test run is \{…\}\.|Latest test run passed\.)$
entries.justification: The decision helper has no production import; only its unit spec calls it. This short-lived exception prevents dormant code from being mistaken for rendered copy while removal or reintegration is coordinated.
These are ModerationResult discriminants used for fail-open control flow and telemetry. Routes expose localized moderation codes/messages, not these internal reason identifiers.
verifyBiometricUnlock has no production caller in the mobile package; these are typed result discriminants asserted only by tests. Reuse must add catalogued user copy before this exception expires.
These are typed availability discriminants in the API contract. Client surfaces select their localized unavailable/upgrade copy from the reason and do not render the raw value.
These typed rate-card discriminants select localized upgrade-plan or unavailable labels in the deployment panel and stable API error codes in the publish handler.
These are CreditGateDecision discriminants. API callers translate each blocked outcome into a catalogued public error contract and never display the raw snake-case value.
These union members are HMAC verification machine outcomes. connector-proxy maps them to localized CONNECTOR_TOKEN_* public codes/messages before replying.
These union members are object-storage HMAC verification machine outcomes. API authorization maps failure to stable localized public contracts and does not render the raw reason.

This internal poll-state reason keeps a missing pod non-terminal until the bounded manager timeout. App-build and scheduled-job callers consume only phase, exitCode and DeadlineExceeded; this text never crosses HTTP.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:crypto mining command pattern|port scanning tool|metadata service access attempt|download and execute pattern|reverse shell pattern|fork bomb pattern|many failed auth attempts|workspace creation spike|excessive AI usage|storage abuse threshold exceeded|CPU abuse threshold exceeded|preview spam threshold exceeded)$
entries.justification: These are canonical backend abuse-classifier evidence labels persisted for audit/SIEM. Public command failures use localized stable error contracts; admin tables render type/severity/status rather than this internal evidence string.

These candidates are nested fragments of private Cloud Build diagnostics. The deploy flow uses them only to determine failure and persists a catalogued DEPLOY_SERVER_FAILED log; raw provider detail and log URL are not returned as UI copy.
These values are low-cardinality auth_failures_total metric labels. Login responses use the locale-aware app-public catalogue and do not expose metric dimensions.

ReleaseManifestOutcome.reason — machine codes persisted verbatim into Deployment.metadata.rollbackUnavailableReason and asserted by the rollback suites. Localising them would corrupt stored data: a row written in French would stop matching a check written in English. User-facing rollback text goes through the locale-aware app-public catalogue.
These are audit metadata, reconciliation state, metrics or storage-fallback dimensions. Every related HTTP failure uses a catalogued code/message; the raw identifiers are never rendered.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Open the project workspace before deploying\.|Workspace is starting — please retry\.)$
entries.justification: readWorkspaceDeployManifest returns these private outcomes only to /deployments/detect, which discards the text and emits publicPendingDeployTarget(locale). They never enter the response payload.

This frame is persisted as internal abuse evidence and delivered to SIEM, not rendered platform copy. User command failures use localized COMMAND_BLOCKED_BY_ABUSE responses; admin review renders the event type/severity/status.

These values are stable AI cost-ledger source identifiers and BYOK policy discriminants. Cost dashboards aggregate provider/model/tokens without rendering reason, while chat consumes policy as machine data.
This response belongs to an internal-secret CronJob endpoint and is consumed only as an operator skip reason. The user database routes return localized FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED copy.

These are typed internal gate/report outcomes. Service shutdown callers inspect the boolean and emit catalogued public errors; Stripe reporting callers ignore the optional reason after operator instrumentation.
These union members are signed OAuth-state verification outcomes. Callback routes map them to localized OAUTH_STATE_EXPIRED/OAUTH_STATE_INVALID contracts and never render the raw value.

These are canonical accounting transaction reason identifiers stored in the private double-entry ledger. No product route or UI reads LedgerTransaction.reason; they are retained for reconciliation and audit tooling.
These uppercase values are stable license-decision codes. Gallery endpoints pair them with locale-aware public error copy; code identifiers intentionally remain invariant.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:no components|\{…\} component snapshot\(s\) unverified|components snapshotted under different logical barriers \(not the same instant\)|promotion \{…\} is \{…\}, not PROMOTION_COMMITTED — an incomplete promotion can never become a release|\{…\} attachment\(s\) not relinked into the tenant repo|Binary Authorization is \{…\}, not PASSED)$
entries.justification: checkpointManifestVisible and releaseMayBeCut have no production caller; only state-machine specs exercise these programmer/audit diagnostics. Reintegration must add a localized boundary before this exception expires.

entries.textPattern: ^(?:Detected a \{…\} server|Static single-page app \(no server\) — deploy as a static site\.|Static site \(index\.html, no server\)\.)$
entries.justification: These are internal detector summaries. publicDetectedDeployTarget rebuilds server/static/unknown reason and error fields from app-public-copy in the request locale; raw detector text is never serialized.
